items.title: Live: Chalmers to target red tape in budget amid warning from business groups
items.description: Cutting red tape and compliance costs will be a focus of next month's federal budget, Treasurer Jim Chalmers says, as a group of businesses call for a slash to regulatory costs in response to the Middle East war. Follow live.

items.description: Welcome to Monday and a return to the rhetorical threat spiral we've been watching for weeks. Here's what you should know this morning.

items.title: Trump says US seized Iranian ship as talks falter

featured_image.name: US Navy Seizes Iranian-Flagged Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman ...

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that American forces had captured an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions just as Washington pushes to restart stalled peace negotiations with Tehran. Hours later, Iran rejected the proposed second round of talks, casting fresh doubt on the prospects for a diplomatic resolution before a fragile ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran refuses to negotiate while US naval blockade remains in place

featured_image.name: US general clarifies Iranian ports under blockade, not Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in effect, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The announcement throws into doubt a planned resumption of diplomacy just days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire on April 22.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Live: US Navy opens fire on an Iranian cargo ship, Trump says
items.description: Donald Trump says the US Navy has opened fire on an Iranian-flagged cargo ship that tried to get through the Strait of Hormuz in an attempt to break the American blockade of the shipping channel. Follow live.

items.title: 'Hard to break the habit': Why free public transport isn't enough to shift from cars
items.description: Free public transport is a popular policy, but researchers say it's not enough to convince drivers to leave the car at home.

items.title: The neighbourhoods where ADHD rates are skyrocketing
items.description: ADHD diagnoses in adults have exploded across Australia since 2017. For the first time, we have the data that shows where it is — and isn't — happening.

items.title: Iran refuses to send negotiators to Pakistan over US naval blockade

featured_image.name: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again over US blockade of its ports

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in place, according to reports from Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The refusal throws into doubt plans announced by President Donald Trump, who said his representatives would arrive in Islamabad on Monday evening to resume negotiations.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Why Celine Cremer's family don't live with anger after remains found in forest
items.description: Backpacker Celine Cremer set off on a short walk with only a phone to guide her — and vanished. More than two years later, her family has an urgent message for other travellers.

items.title: Australia faced the same dilemma as China in 2004 but made the wrong call
items.description: While the rest of us count the cost in higher fuel costs, higher inflation and a weaker economy,  China — the actual winner of the war — will be enjoying a surge of global interest in its solar panels, wind turbines and electric vehicles.

items.title: The government is looking for cuts and thinks it has found its target
items.description: For the first time in this survey, more Australians are dissatisfied with the direction of the country than satisfied. The conflict between the US/Israel and Iran has delivered more than geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: Trump reverses course, confirms Vance will lead Iran talks in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner are in negotiations with Iran in Pakistan

items.description: In a confusing sequence of announcements on Sunday, President Donald Trump initially told ABC News that Vice President JD Vance would not travel to Pakistan for a second round of negotiations with Iran, only for the White House to later confirm that Vance would in fact lead the delegation. The back-and-forth unfolded as the administration scrambled to arrange talks ahead of a fragile ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Angola shrine tied to slave trade
items.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday led a rosary prayer at the Sanctuary of Mama Muxima, a revered Catholic shrine in Angola built by Portuguese colonizers in the late 16th century that served as a hub in the transatlantic slave trade. The visit marked one of the most symbolically charged moments of the American pope's 11-day tour of Africa.[1][2]

items.title: Trump sends envoys to Pakistan for new Iran talks

featured_image.name: Pakistan proposes second round of U.S.-Iran talks as standoff ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of direct negotiations with Iran, with talks set to begin Tuesday, as the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran approaches its April 22 expiration.[1][2]

In an interview with Fox News, Trump warned that if Tehran does not agree to a deal, the whole of Iran will be "blown up," specifically threatening to target bridges and power plants. He demanded that Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.[2][1]

items.title: U.S. backs $50M rare earth project in South Africa to cut China reliance

featured_image.name: US backs a South Africa project to extract rare earths as it ... - AP News

items.description: A U.S.-backed project in South Africa aims to extract rare earth minerals from massive industrial waste dunes, part of a broader push by Washington to loosen China's grip on the critical minerals supply chain.

items.title: Iran regains 60% of missile launchers during ceasefire, US intelligence estimates

featured_image.name: Iran reportedly recovering bombed missile bunkers within ...

items.description: Seven weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, American intelligence and military officials now estimate that Tehran still holds roughly 60 percent of its pre-war missile launchers and about 40 percent of its long-range attack drone arsenal, according to a report by The New York Times published on Friday. The assessment underscores a widening gap between the Trump administration's claims of having devastated Iran's military and the reality on the ground.[1][2][3]

items.title: Penn State develops 3D-printed brain sensors tailored to each patient

featured_image.name: Penn State researchers develop 3D printed bioelectrodes ...

items.description: Researchers at Penn State have unveiled a method for 3D printing soft, stretchable brain electrodes customized to the unique folds of each patient's brain, a development that could reshape how neurological diseases are monitored and treated.

items.title: French peacekeeper killed as Lebanon ceasefire frays

featured_image.name: In southern Lebanon, UN peacekeepers are caught in a vice

items.description: Israeli forces continued shelling and demolition operations across southern Lebanon on Saturday, less than two days after a US-brokered 10-day ceasefire took effect, raising doubts about the durability of the truce even as a French UN peacekeeper was killed in a separate attack attributed to Hezbollah.
